name: Paro Red Rice
description: Nutty, earthy grain from terraced paddies above the Paro chhu. Cooks soft in about 25 minutes, no soaking needed.
storage: Keep in an airtight tin, away from damp. Use within six months.

name: Bumthang Buckwheat Flour
description: Stone-ground from bitter and sweet buckwheat. The base for khuli pancakes and puta noodles.
storage: Store sealed in a cool cupboard. Best within three months of milling.

name: Kharang (Cracked Maize)
description: Sun-dried, cracked maize from the east. Cook with rice or eat it the way grandparents did, with butter tea.
storage: Keep dry and sealed. Lasts many months.

name: Fresh Green Chilli
description: Long, thin-skinned chillies picked in the cool of the morning. The heart of a good ema datshi.
storage: Wrap loosely in paper and refrigerate. Use within a week.

name: Spring Asparagus
description: Thin spears cut by hand along the river valleys in early spring. Only around for a few weeks.
storage: Stand upright in a glass of water in the fridge. Eat within three days.

name: Highland Potatoes
description: Waxy, thin-skinned potatoes from the high valleys. Hold their shape in kewa datshi.
storage: Keep in a dark, airy basket. Do not refrigerate.

name: Seasonal Leafy Greens
description: Mustard greens, spinach and radish leaves, cut close to the day of delivery.
storage: Rinse, shake dry and wrap in a damp cloth. Use within two days.

name: Wild Mushrooms
description: Gathered from the pine forests during the monsoon. Supply depends on the rain, so we confirm each week.
storage: Keep in a paper bag in the fridge. Cook within two days.

name: Tsirang Mandarins
description: Sweet, easy-peel oranges from the warm southern hills. The first boxes arrive in late November.
storage: Keep in a cool, airy place. Do not stack too high.

name: Paro Apples
description: Crisp red apples from small orchards near Drukgyel. Good for eating and for stewing.
storage: Refrigerate in a vented bag. They keep for several weeks.

name: Summer Peaches
description: Small, fragrant peaches from courtyard trees. Soft, so we pack them in single layers.
storage: Ripen on the counter, then refrigerate. Eat within three days.

name: Bumthang Blossom Honey
description: Light, floral honey from hives kept near buckwheat and apple blossom.
storage: Keep at room temperature. It may crystallise in winter. Warm the jar gently and it turns liquid again.

name: Highland Forest Honey
description: Darker and deeper, from hives at the forest edge. A small batch every year.
storage: Keep at room temperature, lid closed.

name: Raw Honeycomb Pieces
description: Cut comb packed in tubs. Bring it to the table with khuli or butter tea.

name: Fresh Datshi Cheese
description: Soft farmhouse cheese, made in small rounds. Melts into ema datshi, kewa datshi and shamu datshi.
storage: Refrigerate and use within five days.

name: Chugo (Hard Yak Cheese)
description: Dried cheese cubes strung on a cord, made by herders in the high pastures. Chew slowly.
storage: Keeps for months in a dry tin.

name: Sun-dried Red Chilli
description: Red chillies dried on rooftops in autumn. Crush into ezay or cook whole through winter.
storage: Keep sealed and dry. Lasts through to the next season.
